quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Keep your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you enter a work zone. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions. Workers may be present.

questions.question: Driving while taking medication that affects your driving is allowed:

options.text: Never.
If you don't feel sleepy.
If a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while taking any substance that makes it unsafe to drive. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to stop safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to stop safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars disappear into a truck's blind spots. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers who want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, look to your:

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians before entering. Check left again because vehicles from the left will be closer. Look across the whole intersection to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: When it is very foggy, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light bounces off water and creates glare, making it harder to see. Fog lights may also help if your car has them.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and alertness. The more alcohol you drink, the worse your judgment and driving skills become. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and other vehicles.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill without a curb, or uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the edge so your car rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so your car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating high-fat foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Only insurance and registration.
Only your license.
Your license, insurance, and registration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license, insurance, and registration.
questions.explanation: You must carry your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must show all three documents when stopped.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park completely off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park completely off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: Move your car completely off the road if it breaks down.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers frustrated about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic away from work hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from work hazards.
questions.explanation: Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests when you approach a work zone. These warn you and guide you.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer right.
Steer left.
Tap brakes and shift to neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens your car.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train. Wait until all gates are up and all signals stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: This sign warns that the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve where the road curves right, then left.

questions.question: This sign shows:

options.text: An intersection.
A road curve.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn of conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns of danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in work areas.

questions.question: A large truck is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may happen?

options.text: The truck can complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
The truck may need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
The truck must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks have a bigger difference between the paths of the front and rear wheels. This means they often need to swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates, disabled veteran license plates, or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane?

options.text: Honk so they know to clear the way.
Give them the right-of-way.
Swerve quickly around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to stop and give the right-of-way to a blind person using a guide dog or carrying a white cane with a red tip. Let them cross safely before you go.

questions.question: When should you not start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: At any time.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: At any time.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic in that lane may cross to pass. A solid yellow line means traffic in that lane cannot cross to pass.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines cannot affect driving if you take the right dose.
Medicines are safe anytime if a doctor prescribed them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, whether prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous and affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You are responsible for knowing how your medicine affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: Your car's wheels have gone off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the wheels slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: If your car leaves the road, hold the steering wheel steady, release the gas pedal, and brake gently. Slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Jerking the wheel can cause you to lose control or hit other lanes.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift to neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, or deep puddles to prevent skidding. The safest surface to drive on is dry and solid.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, you can drive safely.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is necessary to react to things on the road. Even below the legal limit, any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers may cross to change lanes. A solid line means drivers cannot cross. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills to avoid skidding. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down.

questions.question: A traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic light.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they go against traffic laws, signs, or signals.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Stay at your speed and in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, drive to the nearest edge.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.
Where signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleyways. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Pass only where signs and road markings allow it, and only if you have enough space.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving, including cold, allergy, and nerve medicines. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that impairs your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that their vehicle has left the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that their vehicle has left the lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out without looking, or a driver may pull into traffic before seeing you.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange warning signs on a roadway.

questions.question: How can you avoid carbon monoxide poisoning?

options.text: Have your exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.
Keep your engine off when your vehicle is in a closed garage.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide fumes are colorless and deadly. Symptoms include sudden tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. Fresh air is the only cure.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?

options.text: White
Blue
Green

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are white with black markings and drivers must obey them.
